evidence: Zero import-time side effects: no DB connections, file I/O, or network calls at module scope in any of the 4 production files
Acyclic import graph: main.tsx -> App.tsx -> button.tsx -> utils.ts, a simple chain with no circular dependencies
No global singletons or mutable module-level state with ordering concerns across the codebase
No environment variable reads (process.env / import.meta.env) at module scope in any production file
Framework bootstrap (createRoot in main.tsx) is correctly isolated to the single entry-point file
Module-level JSX in scenes array (App.tsx lines 28-212) creates React elements at import time, but this is standard React pattern with no coupling impact at this scale
buttonVariants config computed at import time via cva() is the standard library usage pattern, not a coupling concern

initialization_coupling.dimension_character: The codebase is a small (479 LOC, 4 files) Vite+React application with a trivially simple acyclic import graph and zero initialization coupling patterns. No global singletons, no import-time side effects, no circular dependencies, and no environment variable reads at module scope exist. The only module-scope work is standard React JSX element creation in the scenes array and a CVA variant configuration call, both of which are harmless conventional patterns.
initialization_coupling.score_rationale: Score is 100.0 because the codebase exhibits zero measurable initialization coupling defects across all six rubric criteria. The import dependency tree is a clean linear chain, there are no boot-order dependencies, no mutable shared state across modules, and all framework bootstrap code is properly isolated to the entry point. This is as clean as a codebase of this size can be from an initialization coupling perspective.

add.description: Zero production files perform DB connections, file I/O, or network calls at module scope. This is a strong positive pattern that keeps initialization order-independent and test-friendly.
The import chain (main.tsx -> App.tsx -> button.tsx -> utils.ts) is a simple linear tree with no cycles, hub modules, or conditional/lazy import patterns that could hide circular init dependencies.
There are no module-level mutable global objects whose creation order matters across modules. All state is component-scoped via React hooks, eliminating ordering concerns entirely.

add.header: Framework bootstrap isolated to entry point
add.description: The createRoot call lives exclusively in src/main.tsx, the single framework entry point. No other module performs framework initialization, keeping boot-order predictable.

add.header: No environment variable reads at import time
add.description: No production file reads process.env or import.meta.env at module scope, avoiding the common testing fragility where env-dependent initialization breaks when env vars are absent.

add.header: Module-level JSX in scenes array is benign at this scale
add.description: App.tsx evaluates 6 scene objects with embedded JSX at import time (lines 28-212). While this creates React elements at module scope, the scale is small and this is standard React practice; not a coupling concern.
